items.title: Core registry work is both member service and critical Internet infrastructure
items.summary: RIPE NCC is a not-for-profit membership association and RIR. Its public service scope combines member-facing resource distribution and global public-interest services such as RIPE Database, K-root, DNS, RIPE Atlas, RIPEstat, RIS, and research.
items.implication: The domain should not be modeled as a pure SaaS business. Product strategy must balance member service quality, public trust, registry accuracy, and community legitimacy.

items.title: Routing security is a core adoption loop, not an optional add-on
items.summary: RIPE NCC member updates publicly track IPv4 and IPv6 ROA coverage, LIRs with IPv6, and RPKI-related service signals. RPKI is a global RIR commitment and a practical BGP origin validation control.
items.implication: RPKI, ROA management, RIPEstat, RIS, and training should be linked as one customer journey for routing engineers.

items.title: Policy participation depends on evidence and implementation clarity
items.summary: RIPE NCC operates as secretariat for the RIPE community and provides neutral data sources that can inform policy and governance discussions.
items.implication: Policy support should expose proposal status, impact evidence, and implementation changes rather than treating policy as disconnected documentation.

items.title: Data products serve a broader audience than paying members
items.summary: RIPE Atlas, RIPEstat, RIS, RIPE IPmap, raw datasets, and country reports are public-interest services used by operators, researchers, regulators, and public analysts.
items.implication: Measurement and API product design should prioritize reproducibility, provenance, terms, stability, and responsible reuse.
